interpretations: Count each trader type by the number of advancedbehavior records (rows) that join through to a trader. Share = type count ÷ sum of counts across all types.
Count each trader type by the number of distinct advancedbehavior records (distinct `abhvreg`) that join through to a trader.
Count each trader type by the number of distinct transactions (distinct `transreg`) that have behaviour analyses.
Count each trader type by the number of distinct traders (distinct `tradereg`) that have behaviour analyses.
Treat "exact text matches" as case-sensitive equality on the join keys (`translink` = `transreg`, `trdref` = `tradereg`), using inner joins and dropping unmatched rows.
Treat "exact text matches" as equality after trimming whitespace or ignoring case on the join keys.
Put records whose trader has a NULL `tradekind` in their own group, labelled NULL or "Missing".
Put records whose `tradekind` is NULL or an empty string in the missing group.
Take the average share as the mean of per-type shares, which equals 1 ÷ the number of types (including the missing group).
Take the average share as the mean of per-type shares over only the types that appear after the joins, including the missing group if present.
Take the average share as the mean over all possible `tradekind` enum values (Market Maker, Broker, Individual, Institution), including types with zero count, with the missing group added or not.
Return types whose share is strictly greater than the average share, excluding types equal to it.
Output columns: type, count, share (count ÷ total), and share minus average share.
Report the share as a fraction between 0 and 1.
Report the share as a percentage (×100).
Report the share as unrounded, full-precision values with no rounding or casting.
Return an empty result when the average share is NULL, for example when there are no matching rows.
Return an empty result when the average share is NULL, but treat a zero-row join as producing no output anyway.
Order the output by type name.
Order the output by count or share descending.
Leave the output order unspecified.
Missing interpretations:
Treat the missing group as only NULL `tradekind`, keeping an empty string as its own separate type.
Count each trader type by the number of distinct `trdref` values (distinct traders reached through the transaction link). This is the same as distinct traders, so it is already covered.
Compute the average share as the mean of the shares over only the types that have a nonzero count, so a type with no rows is not included.
Compute the average share as the total of the shares divided by the number of types, so that it equals 1 ÷ the number of types and may be reported as an exact fraction.
Return the share minus the average share as a signed difference, with no absolute value taken.
Treat the "missing" check as applying to the join result, so a missing type is created only by a NULL `tradekind` on a matched trader, never by an unmatched trader.
Treat the output column "count" as an integer count and "share" as a decimal numeric type. Use floating-point division rather than integer division, so the shares are not truncated to 0.
Do not filter on `casestat` or on any compliance table, so only `advancedbehavior`, `transactionrecord` and `trader` are used.
Return no rows when the total count is zero, because a zero denominator makes the shares undefined.
queries:
SELECT t.tradekind,
       COUNT(*) AS cnt,
       COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share
FROM advancedbehavior ab
JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg
JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
GROUP BY t.tradekind;

SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT a.abhvreg) AS record_count
FROM advancedbehavior a
JOIN transactionrecord tr ON a.translink = tr.transreg
JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
GROUP BY t.tradekind;

SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) AS transaction_count
FROM trader t
JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
JOIN advancedbehavior ab ON ab.translink = tr.transreg
GROUP BY t.tradekind

SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT t.tradereg) AS trader_count
FROM trader t
JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
JOIN advancedbehavior ab ON ab.translink = tr.transreg
GROUP BY t.tradekind
